why_next: The transaction executed cleanly, produced valid measurement, and still left the architecture question unmade, and the reason is now precisely located in the design rather than in the arms. Three things it measured are real and new. First, the parent handoff's highest-priority unknown is now closed in its negative form: the shipped declared-vocabulary binder executed 500 read, update and delete operations against a collection that appears in zero of its 600 training observations, all at bind confidence 1.0, all HTTP 200, all verified, with the safety guard passing, for a semantic false-accept of 1.000 rather than the 0.0 the parent packet could only record as unmeasured. That is the liability the architecture most needed bounded, and it is bounded now. Second, the parent's second blocked question, the cost ratio, received its first non-degenerate answer: the re-derivation-to-inherited-execution ratio really was manipulated from 3.0 to 60.0 and the variability binder's break-even against within-episode reuse fell strictly monotonically 2328, 1929, 1274, 814, 473, ending the two-cycle deadlock caused by a cheap regime that was analytically forced rather than measured. Third, a genuine mechanism-versus-matcher separation exists on the discriminating frame: the variability binder bound 250 of 250 held-out in-support identifiers and executed none of the out-of-support ones, and all three structural nulls failed at 0.000. And yet the packet cannot advance the claim, for a reason that is worth more than the numbers: reading the raw rows shows that the ONLY never-observed collection in the test set is scored as an error every time it is bound, so the frozen semantic-guard metric is perfectly maximized by a binder that refuses everything it has not seen, and the variability binder is exactly such a binder. The same closed-set gate that produces the impressive 0.000 false-accept is the gate that makes the mechanism unable to do the transfer C-PARAM-INHERIT exists to enable, and the only cell in which the incumbent binds an unseen collection is the same cell the design scores as an error. So the packet's headline is really a statement about a refusal policy wearing the clothes of a mechanism result, and a design that cannot distinguish 'bound correctly from evidence' from 'refused everything' will certify any future binder for the same reason. The next question therefore cannot be another arm, a wider interval, or another cost-ratio sweep, all of which would refine numbers whose referent is still wrong. It has to make the two obligations compete: force a binder to bind a collection it has never seen, and force it at the same time to refuse a well-formed identifier that is unjustifiable for the collection actually requested, so that a support model is judged on both at once. That is materially different from what this packet ran, it is the question three of the last four Product packets were circling without being able to ask, it is in-lane, it needs only the substrate class that has actually produced valid measurement, and either outcome changes the architecture. It also carries the preconditions this packet exposed and did not fix: a degeneracy guard that fires on a treatment arm, a lexical null whose frozen tie rule is underdetermined, an induction budget that the frozen documents contradict by a factor of nine, and a freeze gate that cannot bind code so F8 is unevaluable.

unknown: Whether ANY slot-support model can bind a collection absent from its training at a useful rate while simultaneously refusing a well-formed but unjustifiable identifier. This is the question the whole packet turns on and it is untouched: the frozen test set contains no task in which binding an unseen collection is correct, and the frozen metric therefore rewards refusal unconditionally. Until that construct exists, neither the incumbent's 1.0 nor the variability binder's 0.0 can be converted into an architecture.

Whether the incumbent's 1.0 rate of executing well-formed identifiers of an unobserved collection persists when the requested collection IS seen and the identifier is a well-formed sibling of a different collection, for example a widget identifier requested inside the seen 'items' collection. No row in this packet tests it, because every recorded abstention reason concerns slot s0 and every out-of-support task varies the collection. This is the residual risk that a collection-level closed set does not cover, and it is the cheapest remaining probe in Product.

Whether the variability binder has an identifier-level guard at all. mechanisms.json records s1 support as kind shape '[a-z]+-[0-9]+' with prefixes ['item','order','product'], but no raw row exercises a shape-conforming identifier whose prefix belongs to another collection, so whether the prefix set is enforced at bind time is not established by this evidence.

The cost of the refusal policy, which nobody measured: A1 abstained on 50 percent of tasks by test construction, so the packet contains no estimate of how often a real binder would refuse requests a product would have served, and no estimate of the revenue or task-completion cost of that refusal. Any product claim built on the 0.0 false-accept is currently unpriced on the other side of the ledger.

Whether the monotone break-even curve survives a realistic cost basis. Three of the four cost terms in C-PRODUCT-ECON's own title -- retrieval, verification, maintenance -- were not measured in any arm, the environment records model_calls 0, model_tokens 0, api_key_present false, browser_available false and embedding_service unavailable, and the per-task basis is a self-authored deterministic executor counting HTTP requests. Whether the ratio sensitivity that was finally demonstrated survives those terms is untested.

Whether the mechanism generalizes beyond a single route template and a single identifier shape: multi-template routes, nested resources, path parameters with heterogeneous cardinality, query-parameter identity, or POST-body identity are all outside this frozen design and outside this substrate's validity history (result.json.validity_notes[9], audit.unresolved[0]).

Whether any of this transfers across sites (C-CROSSSITE) or through an LLM agent (C-LLM-INHERIT). Both remain at HYPOTHESIS, both need substrate that is not present, and the smallest unblocking action for either is a model credential or a permitted multi-site corpus. This packet measured the kernel mechanism in isolation with no model in the loop.

Do not read the mechanism result as a general statement about binders. It is one route template /${collection}/${id}, one synthetic identifier shape [a-z]+-[0-9]+, three collection values, a deterministic stdlib server, and a closed set of cardinality 3 used as the guard. A closed set of three learned values is a memorization gate, and the packet contains no evidence about how such a gate behaves on a namespace with thousands of members, on multi-template routes, on query-parameter or body identity, or on nested resources.

Do not assume C-PRODUCT-ECON advanced. It is HELD AT HYPOTHESIS, its registry status, with next_gate 'end-to-end amortized economics on real agents'. The measured sub-result is banked: the cost ratio was really manipulated 3.0 to 60.0 and the break-even against within-episode scratchpad fell strictly monotonically 2328 to 473. Do not treat the incumbent's 1.000 out-of-support execution as a measured harm rate, and do not treat the variability binder's 0.000 as a measured safety guarantee. The audited 'margin 1.0' on Frame B is arithmetic, not significance. Non-degenerate intervals require a wider identifier distribution, not more arms (result.json.validity_notes[10]).

On Frame R the goal literally contains the identifier and the collection token, so the lexical-overlap null flips between 0.000 and 1.000 on the undeclared tie order alone, and a pure string matcher is expected to succeed. Frame B is the discriminating frame and the request designated it supplementary, which is backwards.
